evidence.finding: _scatter_add_sort_key_kernel 806.2us, _scatter_add_sort_out_kernel 599.8us (target case 1.4008ms). Per-block means split by kernel: sort_key aiv_time 15.377us / aiv_vec_time 14.030us / aiv_vec_ratio 0.913, mte2_ratio 0.045, mte3_ratio 0.022, scalar_ratio 0.086, vec_wait_ratio 0.026, vec_total_cflt_ratio 0.124; sort_out aiv_time 11.638us / aiv_vec_ratio 0.857. Both kernels are vector-ALU saturated; memory lanes and scalar are nearly empty, so the only lever on this path is fewer/cheaper vector instructions.

Normalized partial-window timeline of the same sort_key kernel (absolute_time_qualified=false): VECTOR productive_ratio 0.907, wait_only_ratio 0.026, idle_ratio 0.067; SCALAR productive 0.024 but wait_only 0.688 (explicit WAIT_FLAG on PIPE:VEC); MTE2 productive 0.051 (0.635us of a 12.366us window); MTE3 productive 0.017; CACHEMISS productive 0.005. The hotspot regions rank the source_function body (356 instr, 53.16us instruction-sum) and, inside it, the static loop at source lines 206-210 (the segmented-prefix loop, 366 instr, 36.46us instruction-sum, 5.28 of 5.44us trace-union). Top individual instructions are BAR/WAIT_FLAG at lines 198/199/201/202 and in that loop, each ~4.0-4.5us.

The lowered key kernel contains 11 unrolled scan steps; each step emits two `tt.gather` (previous_target on a shifted lane vector, then previous_sum on the shifted segment-sum vector) plus cmp/andi/select/addf. That is 22 `tt.gather` in the scan on top of the one `tt.gather` used to permute values into sorted order, i.e. 23 full-width cross-lane permutes per row, while the only other work is one `ascend.sort`, a handful of int ops and two contiguous stores.

The output kernel already performs a LOG+1 = 12-step on-chip binary search over the stored sorted keys plus 2 gathers for run-end/prefix lookup; it is the cheaper of the two kernels (11.638us/block) and is where run start (`lo`) and run end (`end`) are already known exactly.

Retained best: all 18 formal cases PASSED, geo_mean 2.0936, min speedup 1.8075; correctness-8 abs_err 2.38e-7 / rel_err 1.69e-6 with matched_ratio 1.0 required, so any change to fp32 summation order must stay far inside atol/rtol 1e-4.

hypothesis: On the wide-row sorted-segment path the key kernel's cost is dominated by the 11-step segmented prefix scan, which is lowered to 22 full-width cross-lane tt.gather ops plus the associated barrier/select chain. The scan exists only to produce per-run sums at run ends; the out kernel already computes every run's start `lo` and end `end` by binary search. Replacing the segmented scan with one whole-vector inclusive prefix sum (tl.cumsum) and computing each run's sum in the out kernel as prefix[end-1] - prefix[lo-1] removes 22 gathers from the expensive kernel at the cost of one extra gather in the cheaper kernel.
change: candidate.py only, sorted-segment path: (1) _scatter_add_sort_key_kernel stores tl.cumsum(sv, axis=0) into prefix_ptr and drops the 11-step double-gather segmented scan and its now-unused `targets` vector; (2) _scatter_add_sort_out_kernel subtracts the prefix at the run start it already knows: before = gather(prefix, max(lo-1,0)) zeroed when lo==0, delta = where(end > lo, after - before, 0). No change to launch geometry, grid, allocation shapes (keys/prefix stay (rows,B) fp32), the dense owner path, the atomic path, the generic N-d path or the fp32-accumulate/one-rounding-on-store semantics.
expected: sort_key per-block aiv_vec_time 14.03us -> ~7-9us and kernel duration 806us -> ~500-620us; sort_out 599.8us -> ~610-630us; target case ~1.40ms -> ~1.15-1.25ms (about 1.12-1.22x on that case, the same relative gain on the 1024x1024 and fp16/bf16 wide cases). VECTOR productive share of sort_key should stay high (still vector-bound) but with a much smaller instruction count.
validation: Bridge preflight on the new candidate (compile + 21 supplementary), then host formal evaluation of all 18 cases: require all PASSED, matched_ratio 1.0, geo_mean and every timing case >= the retained 2.0936 / per-case values, no change on the dense (<=256 cols) and generic paths, and correctness errors inside atol/rtol 1e-4 (expected fp32 error from the prefix-subtraction reformulation ~1e-6..1e-5, i.e. bounded by eps * row-prefix magnitude, ~20x below tolerance).
alternatives: tl.associative_scan with the already-present _segment_combine monoid: keeps bit-identical per-run tree sums and removes the gathers, but depends on backend support/lowering quality for associative_scan on this target, so a compile failure would cost a round trip without a perf signal.

Merge the two kernels into a single per-row program to avoid the 64MB keys/prefix round trip: rejected because MTE2 0.045 + MTE3 0.022 occupancy shows the round trip is ~7% and pipelined, while the loss is vector issue occupancy.

Keep the two-gather scan but load `previous_target` from the already-stored sorted keys instead of re-gathering a converted int vector: still one cross-lane read per step, only halves the gather count, strictly less than the cumsum reformulation.
Dense destination-owned kernel for the whole range: rejected, its ncols-wide compare costs 2.85ms at 1024 columns per the documented measurement.
discriminating_observation: If the scan's gathers are the cost, sort_key vector time must fall (806us -> roughly 520-620us) while sort_out rises by only the single added prefix gather (599.8us -> ~610-630us), and the BAR cluster attributable to source lines 206-210 must disappear from the next hotspot/timeline capture. If instead sort dominates the vector time (gathers cheap), sort_key duration will stay near 806us and only the instruction mix will change.
